subject: Clarifying: do you train on customer data? EU residency & retention details
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@alphacorp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick Q: do you train models on customer inputs? + residency details

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Before we move to SOW approval I have a couple of security questions from our InfoSec team (summary below). Can you confirm these are accurate for Redwood's hosted API?

1) "Do you train or fine-tune Redwood models on customer-provided inputs (prompts or responses)?"
2) Data residency: can we guarantee EU-only processing & storage for AlphaCorp customer data?
3) Retention windows: logs, request/response payloads, embeddings — what are default retention periods and are they contractually adjustable?

I've attached our standard security questionnaire (Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) and flagged the relevant items. If this is easier, can you loop in your security/compliance contact or provide standard clause text we can use in the SOW?

Appreciate a short, actionable answer so I can move this to legal.

—Alex
Alex Li
Head of Product Security, AlphaCorp

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@alphacorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: do you train models on customer inputs? + residency details

Hi Alex — great questions, thank you. Short answers up front, then a brief breakdown with where we can make contractual guarantees.

Short answers:
- We do not use customer inputs from the Hosted API to train or fine-tune public models by default.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data stays isolated and is never used for model training.
- Default retention (hosted): request/response payloads are retained for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection; embeddings are retained 90 days unless you opt into longer retention for caching/performance.
- EU residency: we can route and store AlphaCorp data to our EU region and document that in the SOW for EU-only processing.

Details and nuance:
1) Training usage:
  - Hosted API: We have a default operational telemetry pipeline that collects logs and anonymized usage metrics to monitor service quality. We do not feed raw customer prompts/responses into model training datasets for our public models unless a customer explicitly opts in to a "help improve models" program.
  - Dedicated: Data is isolated in your reserved capacity and not used for any model training.
  - Private (on-prem/VPC): fully customer-controlled; Redwood has no access for training.

2) Retention:
  - Request/response payloads: 30 days (default). Shorter/longer retention is configurable under Dedicated/Private; for Hosted customers we can add an addendum for 0/7/30-day retention options depending on your compliance needs.
  - Embeddings and cached artifacts: 90 days by default for Hosted (used to speed repeat queries).
  - Audit logs / billing records: retained per contract (typically 1–7 years depending on the plan).

3) EU residency:
  - We can ensure processing and storage in an EU region (Frankfurt/Belgium depending on availability) and restrict backups to EU-only. This can be captured as a contractual commitment with scope and exceptions (e.g., customer-initiated export).

Next steps I recommend:
- I can share a short SOW clause and an NDA-friendly security appendix that explicitly states "no training on customer inputs" for the hosted environment and the retention windows we discussed.
- Looping in Neha (cc) who handles contracts & SLA customizations — she can draft the clause and coordinate with your legal team.

Attaching our public doc link as well: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/data-residency-retention. If helpful I can also get Marissa from legal on a quick call.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Li <alex.li@alphacorp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-legal@alphacorp.com
Date: 2026-01-15T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: do you train models on customer inputs? + residency details

Thanks Jonas — that helps. Our legal team would like two things before we proceed with signatures:

1) A copy of your SOC 2 report or equivalent, and confirmation of the retention/processing commitments in writing.
2) A proposed SOW paragraph (exact wording) that we can include in our procurement SOW. We want a clear, machine-readable guarantee that data will not be used for model training and that EU data will remain in-region.

I've included a draft SOW in our internal format (AlphaCorp_SOW_draft.docx) — attaching for reference. Can you have Neha or your legal team propose the exact text?

—Alex

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@alphacorp.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-16T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: do you train models on customer inputs? + residency details

Alex — appreciate the clarity. Neha/Marissa, looping you both to propose contract language and provide the SOC2 artifact.

Proposed SOW language (draft for legal review):
"Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, embeddings, and any derived artifacts) to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's public models or services without the Customer's explicit, documented opt-in. Customer Data shall be processed and stored exclusively within the European Union when the Customer elects EU residency in writing. Retention: request/response payloads will be retained for thirty (30) days by default; embeddings and cached artifacts will be retained for ninety (90) days by default. The parties may agree to alternative retention periods in a separate data retention addendum."
Additional notes:
- We will provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; Marissa, can you confirm availability and the NDA process?
- For AlphaCorp's procurement flow, we can add a short checkbox in the SOW that elects "EU-only processing" and pins retention to 30/90 unless changed.

Alex, if that language looks reasonable I can have Neha produce a redline-ready SOW paragraph and Marissa will route the SOC2 under a short mutual NDA. If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to close this.

Regards,
Jonas
